counterevidence: The 19 states were selected because the retained candidate lost WDL on them; they are not an unbiased sample of training or play.
The probe does not update weights and therefore cannot establish that suppressing these bonuses improves a learned policy.
The prior training logs show that mill formation is dense in winning trajectories, so disabling all mill shaping remains unsupported.
The probe does not address conversion failures, repetition draws, fifty-move draws, architecture, curriculum, or delayed credit.

hypothesis.statement: Suppressing immediate mill shaping only when the complete logical turn downgrades corrected Malom WDL may reduce premature mill closure without removing the useful value-preserving mill signal.
hypothesis.support: All 16 mill-forming frozen downgrade turns receive +0.25 in legacy mode and zero in malom-preserving-only mode; all non-mill turns remain zero and the action and successor state are identical.
hypothesis.next_test: Run a matched legacy-unconditional versus malom-preserving-only learning smoke with identical seed, data, curriculum, baseline, update count and held-out evaluator.

observed_facts: All 19 frozen first-downgrade turns replay as complete legal turns to their committed successor FEN.
Live sector-corrected-v1 Malom reproduces the committed downgrade quality on all 19 states.
Sixteen states form a mill and receive a total +4.0 legacy shaping reward.
Malom-preserving-only and disabled modes both award zero on these value-downgrading turns.
The preserving-only result equals disabled only because this cohort contains only downgrades; fixed tests separately prove that preserving mills retain the bonus.
No candidate model, optimizer, new action selection, new game, or weight update was used.
